- YAML duplicate-key repair removes entries only when their complete contents match. Conflicting block scalars, nested mappings and multiline values remain invalid for the existing correction/retry flow. Ambiguous flow and quoted nodes stay byte-for-byte unchanged while unrelated complete duplicates can still be removed; retained bodies keep repeated literal lines, and malformed continuation after a dedented comment stays invalid.
- Closed YAML flow values such as `[EPIC-1]` and `{owner: model}` no longer disable unrelated duplicate-key or nested-mapping repairs. Ordinary blank separators remain outside duplicate entries; scalar whitespace keeps its meaning, and malformed continuations are left untouched.
- Malformed `free_text` values such as `|some prose` and `>some prose` are quoted as literal text. Valid block-scalar headers keep their existing meaning, and reserved-indicator repairs retain their separate rules.
- Nested-mapping indentation repair preserves literal block contents, including explicit indentation indicators and text that resembles mapping keys or comments.
- Fixed structured-output parsing changing valid YAML before it had a reason to repair it. Nested sequences stay nested, explicit nested-mapping recovery still runs, and malformed siblings still receive only the repairs they need. The structured-output parser normalizes Windows line endings before line-based repairs, and list-item block scalars keep sibling fields outside their bodies.
- Fixed XML-looking lines inside literal YAML blocks being removed or named in warnings when they were never removed. Only tag-only lines outside a block are stripped, and warnings name the tags actually removed.
- Fixed parser diagnostics choosing a legacy alias based on payload order or disappearing inside refinement and coverage parsing. Canonical literal field spellings now win regardless of payload order, disagreements remain visible as warnings, duplicate file-effect warnings are emitted once, uppercase code fences are accepted, and invalid bead iteration or blank status values are reported instead of being silently coerced.
- Fixed the parser cache retaining a result after its repair code changed. Its cache key now fingerprints the complete shared repair and structured-output parser sources without reading source files at runtime.
- Slow or incomplete Cancel and Finish Without Merge uploads no longer hold the merge lock. Payload validation finishes before locking, then current ticket state is checked before any action.
- Ticket GET requests no longer contact GitHub, update PR artifacts, or complete merges. A daemon-owned poller checks waiting tickets at startup and about every 30 seconds after each sweep, retries failed checks with per-ticket delays capped at five minutes, and resumes after restart. Shutdown stops scheduling and drains the active check within the process shutdown deadline before closing storage. A successful merge report lets restart finish the workflow without repeating remote completion.
- Verified merge checkpoints cannot be overwritten by cancellation or finishing without merge. Recovery repairs stale PR metadata, validates the recorded PR identity, and keeps the checkpoint available if later finalization fails.
- An unreadable attached project no longer prevents healthy projects from detecting merged PRs. Invalid GitHub metadata produces an advisory retry instead of silently resetting backoff; requests pin the API contract that supplies the landed commit.
- Polling reads only waiting ticket references and releases the ticket lock during GitHub state reads, so slow reads do not delay Cancel or Finish Without Merge. A failed advisory log cannot stop checks for other tickets. PR reports retain their generation timestamp and label generated content separately from live GitHub state.
- External squash and rebase merges are verified using the commit GitHub records as landed on the remote base. The PR head must still match the approved candidate, so later unapproved changes cannot pass completion. Checks use the stored PR number even after its branch is deleted. Merge requests include the approved SHA so GitHub rejects a head changed between checking and merging.
- Cleanup cannot be canceled after the finish decision is recorded. A repeated Merge request returns success when verified completion is already recorded; canceled, blocked and unrelated states still reject it.
- Mock workflow dispatch explicitly covers inactive states, preventing them from falling through to live execution when the workflow gains a state.
- Background detection and the Merge action share completion logic and a per-ticket lock with close and cancel. Background checks only finish PRs already merged on GitHub; failures remain advisory and keep the ticket waiting. The explicit Merge action retains its existing failure response and blocked status.
- Isolated the package-import regression check in its own integration worker and reused one subprocess for both assertions, reducing Windows subprocess contention while retaining failure detection and cleaning up temporary files.
- PowerShell runtime launchers preserve a single program argument as an argument, instead of splitting it into characters. Windows launcher tests use one case-insensitive PATH entry and fixed shell commands; AI-question tests wait for timer hydration, and authentication tests initialize their database and require successful authorized responses.
- Manual QA event reads and version discovery no longer depend on an unrelated `v1` directory being intact. Worktree size previews skip final aliases without following them, and an unreadable log no longer prevents recovery of the remaining logs on the same ticket.
- Unsafe ticket size and approval requests return HTTP 400 without advancing approval state. Folder opening also reports targets removed or replaced before launch as invalid paths. Missing bead trackers during planning no longer produce read-failure warnings.
- Fixed approving a bead plan that needs editing being reported as a server fault. A bead with no test command and no reason for having none can be saved and offered for approval, and the refusal that follows now says the plan cannot be approved as written and names the bead, instead of a generic failure that sends you to the logs.
- Fixed the beads approval editor dropping test commands written in the older plain-text form. The editor cannot show them and the browser cannot know which shell they belong to, so it now declines to edit those beads and points at the JSONL tab, rather than saving the plan without commands nobody touched.
- Fixed a retry resuming the wrong bead when a timestamp is unreadable. A damaged `updatedAt` hid a good `startedAt` beside it, and the bead was treated as having no timestamp at all, so recovery fell back to counting retries instead of using the time the work actually happened.
- Fixed the artifact view printing a bead's context guidance as raw JSON when the bead simply has none. Every saved plan carries an empty guidance record, and the viewer showed that record instead of leaving the section out.
- Fixed a bead plan being read differently by every surface that reads it, depending on which spelling its fields were stored under. Bead files carry two spellings of most fields (`blockedBy` beside `blocked_by`, `acceptance_criteria` beside `acceptanceCriteria`), and each screen and each step recognised its own subset. The same bead showed its dependencies in the editor and none in the artifact view or the outline; an issue type stored the older way fell back to a default in the editor; and, worst of it, the runtime recognised the fewest of all, so a plan that read correctly on the approval screen could be approved and then never run, crash the coding step, block its own retry with a false reason, resume the wrong bead, or lose its Manual QA evidence with nothing said. Every accepted spelling is now written down once and read the same way by every screen, by approval, and by the runtime, with a test that holds the interface's list and the runtime's to each other. Saving a plan writes each field once, under the spelling the runtime reads, while keeping any field the editor does not touch.
- Fixed an interrupted bead-plan edit being restored over a file that has since changed. A draft saved before the tracker was damaged (or before someone else repaired it) came back as though it were the file on disk, and saving it wrote over the change. A draft is now restored only onto the file it was typed against; otherwise the screen shows what is actually stored. Saving also leaves the editor holding what was just written, instead of the pre-save draft coming back as unsaved changes against a file that already has them.
- Fixed the beads approval screen reporting a different line number from the server for the same damaged row, and losing every intact bead in a tracker whose *first* line is damaged.
- Fixed a refused save leaving nowhere to go: when the tracker changed underneath a draft, the screen kept showing the old file with no way to see the new one. It now offers to reload it, and keeps the draft.
- Fixed the beads approval screen dropping rows that are valid JSON but not beads. A stored `null`, a list, or an object with no id was absent from the structured editor with nothing said, and a save wrote the file back without it: the same loss a damaged line used to cause, one step further along. Those lines are now named beside the damaged ones, the structured editor is withdrawn while any exist, and approval waits until every line reads as a bead. Guidance stored as anything other than pattern lists is refused the same way, whichever spelling it is under.
- Fixed the YAML repairs rewriting text inside a literal block. Model output written as a block scalar (a description, a rationale, an answer) was scanned as ordinary YAML by repairs that did not recognise the block, so a body line came back reformatted, split in two, re-indented or quoted. Every repair now leaves that text alone, in every form the block can be opened with: an explicit indentation width, a trailing comment, and a block written as a list entry.
- Fixed the beads approval editor silently replacing context guidance written as free text with empty pattern lists. That guidance has no field in the structured editor, so it now says which beads carry it and points at the JSONL tab, the way it does for a line it could not parse.
- Fixed unreadable bead tracker files hiding healthy rows or falsely reducing a generated verification checklist. Diagnostic projections keep their surviving rows and expose the read error, while authoritative and checklist reads remain fail-closed.
- Fixed the approval editor rejecting ordinary sequential edits to command arguments. Each argument now has its own literal text control, preserving spaces, newlines and temporarily incomplete values without guessing at shell syntax.
- Bead-editor list fields expose their numbered accessible names without the shared group heading overriding them.
- Fixed approval requests being blocked when optional UI-state data fails to load. Approval uses the fetched bead content hash and remains available when that unrelated request is unavailable.
- Fixed persisted Manual QA repair candidates being treated as current after a schema change. Legacy schema versions regenerate instead of being interpreted as a newer checklist.
- Fixed runtime-only retry and finalisation note aliases being lost when older bead writers use snake_case spellings.
- Fixed `GET /api/tickets/:id/beads` failing the whole request when a single line of the tracker would not parse. One damaged row emptied the beads approval screen, which is the one moment where seeing the rest of the plan is what lets someone repair the file. The route now returns the beads that parsed and reports the line numbers that did not in an `X-Malformed-Lines` response header: the numbers as they are in the file, blank lines counted, so they can be opened and fixed. The approval screen now shows which lines are damaged, keeps the file's own text in its JSONL editor so they can be repaired in place, and refuses to approve (or to save from the structured editor, which holds only the beads that parsed) until the whole file reads. Saving a bead plan also now carries the hash of the file it was built on, and the server refuses a write built on a stale read instead of overwriting whatever landed in between. The client half of this landed earlier, in the artifact viewer's bead filter.
- Fixed the installer wrapper reporting the wrong exit status when it is stopped. `install.sh` forwards an interrupt to the install it started so the caller sees what that install decided; if the install exited before the wrapper looked again, the wrapper reported the signal instead, which is what a supervisor or a CI job reads as "killed" rather than "exited 3".
- Fixed four artifact views crashing on valid JSON of the wrong shape. The pre-flight report, the relevant-files scan, the final test results and the bead list each cast a parsed payload straight to the shape they expected and read its fields unchecked, so content like `{"status":"pending"}`, a `null` list entry or a malformed Manual QA origin threw while rendering instead of falling through to the raw view behind it. Inside the artifact panel that showed an error in place of the artifact; on the approval screens, which are not wrapped in one, it took the whole app to the crash screen.
- Fixed the beads approval outline failing to draw when the stored tracker holds a damaged entry, and repeating a bead id confusing the list that renders it.
- Fixed a bead artifact losing every bead to one damaged entry. The client now skips the bad entry and keeps the rest, which is what the server has always done when reading the file itself, whichever of the three ways the artifact is stored; and content that is not bead-shaped falls back to raw text instead of rendering as invented beads.
- Fixed the coding view's log scroll position going stale after switching bead or iteration. Its scroll listener stayed attached to the replaced viewport, so the jump-to-top and back-to-bottom controls stopped reflecting where the log actually was.
- Fixed a Manual QA checklist with an unreadable generation timestamp rendering it as "Invalid Date", and repeated headings in a generated pull-request body confusing the list that renders them.
- Fixed the artifact viewer accepting a PRD draft the shared parser rejects. Its local reader required only an `epics` array, where the shared one requires the `artifact: prd` marker and at least one titled epic, so the same draft rendered as a structured document in the viewer and was refused at approval. A draft that does not satisfy the shared parser now falls through to the plain-text view, where the raw tab still shows exactly what the model produced.
- Fixed the check that proves the interface builds its execution-setup envelope from the shared constant reading a file the envelope had moved out of. It now names the file the code lives in and fails if that file is ever empty, rather than passing on a read that found nothing.
- Fixed the third-party notices workflow being able to commit notices generated from one commit onto a different one, which left the pull request failing its own licence check. Both halves now work from the same pinned commit, and the push stops if the branch moved.
- Fixed the workflow that regenerates third-party notices running a pull request's own code with a write credential available to it. It ran on any branch whose name began with `renovate/`, and a branch name is chosen by whoever pushes the branch. The build now runs with no credentials at all and hands its one output file to a second job that never runs branch code; that job validates the download as exactly one top-level regular `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` before copying it. The workflow only runs for pull requests Renovate itself opened.
- Fixed the published-install smoke test stopping a daemon it never started. Its teardown ran `looptroop stop` against whatever the machine had on its PATH, so a container leg (which installs no launcher at all) and any leg whose install failed shut down whatever was already running there. It now stops only the launcher that run installed and started.
- Fixed two lifecycle checks in the install smoke test reporting an exit code and discarding the output that says why. Every other check in that file already reported both.
- Fixed the `verify:readonly` command promising something it did not do. It ran the read-only install check without the environment variable that makes the check enforce anything, so it skipped the mount test and exited zero. The command is gone; CI and the release workflow invoke the script directly, with the variable set, which is the only form that verifies anything.
- Fixed the anonymous container check leaving a copy of the real Docker configuration, credentials included, in a temporary directory if it was interrupted while building its credential-free copy. It now removes that directory on any exit, resolves symlinks so it can never write through one into the real configuration, and clears the other environment variables that can supply credentials or point the client at a different daemon.
- Fixed the trusted-executable check trusting the entire working directory when a Windows environment variable was present but empty, which a trimmed container image produces. It also no longer trusts the hosted tool cache, which looks like system infrastructure but is written by ordinary build steps.
- Fixed the WinGet submission leaving its temporary clone behind on the two paths that finish early. That clone's git configuration holds the submission token, so the cleanup it skipped was credential cleanup.
- Fixed the trusted-executable check accepting any directory whose name merely began with a trusted one, so a `gh` placed in `/usr/bin-of-mine` passed as though it were in `/usr/bin`. It now matches by path segment. The check also covers the scripts that push to the Homebrew tap, the Scoop bucket and WinGet, and its Windows roots come from the environment rather than assuming the system drive is C.
- Fixed published smoke checks selecting an extensionless Windows shim from the first `where` result. They now use the same PATHEXT-aware resolver as other tool launches.
- Fixed published smoke checks treating a reworded human-readable `doctor` detail as a channel change. They now compare `checks[].install.channel` and `checks[].install.upgradeCommand` from structured output.
- Fixed the WinGet submission description omitting its declared Git and GitHub CLI dependencies.
- Fixed Scoop bootstrap steps using an implicit installer URL. CI now names `https://get.scoop.sh` explicitly.
- Fixed the WinGet submission printing its own credential when a git command failed, since the token is embedded in the clone URL it reports.
- Fixed `gh` and `choco` being resolved from PATH in the jobs that edit a release and publish to a package feed, so the first matching directory decided which program received those credentials. Both are now resolved once from a directory the runner owns, with a deliberate override for runners that keep them elsewhere.
- Fixed four packaging checks reading their own failure as a passing result. Asking WinGet whether a submission was already open treated an authentication or network failure as "nothing is open", after which the release opened a second pull request against a repository we do not own. The anonymous container check established that it had no credentials by logging out and ignoring whether the logout worked, so a private image could pass a test about whether it is public; it now runs under a configuration built with every credential and credential helper removed, and changes nothing on the machine. The dependency check recorded "everything is up to date" when `npm outdated` could not run at all, and now says it could not check. And republishing a package channel took the commit recorded in a release manifest and checked it out in the jobs that hold the publishing credentials, without ever asking GitHub whether that commit is what the release is tagged at.
- Fixed `npm outdated --json` errors written to stdout by npm 12 being read as a package list. A top-level error or an empty result with a failing status now remains unavailable, while a successful empty object still means the dependencies are current.
- Fixed the throwaway Homebrew tap used by the formula audit and the channel smoke test deleting a real tap of the same name. It removed the directory before building, and again afterwards, with nothing distinguishing its own from anybody else's. It now leaves a marker when it creates one, refuses to replace a directory without that marker, and removes only what it made.
- Fixed `--expect-sha256=<hex>` silently disabling the Chocolatey package's integrity check. The gate tested for the flag with an exact string match, which the `=` spelling never matches, so writing it that way packed whatever bytes were on disk and reported success. That script now reads its arguments through the shared parser like the rest.
- Fixed the release argument parser accepting inherited JavaScript property names as options, so `--constructor` and `--__proto__` passed the check whose only job is to refuse options it does not know. A switch repeated twice, and a single-dash token where a value belongs, are now refused too, and the two scripts that take options only no longer ignore a stray argument.
- Fixed the release scripts accepting a malformed command line and acting on it. An unknown flag was dropped rather than refused, so a typo ran the default behaviour and reported success; a flag whose value was missing fell back to its default; and a flag followed by another flag took that flag as its value, so `--out --foo` wrote to a file literally named `--foo`. All six release and packaging scripts now declare the options they accept and refuse anything else. These command lines are assembled by a workflow from expressions that can expand to nothing, so each of those shapes was reachable rather than hypothetical.
- Fixed release channel input rendering accepting an unsafe manifest asset name. Asset names are now checked as safe basenames before they reach workflow arguments or package descriptors.
- Fixed the release drafter treating every lookup failure as "no release exists yet". An expired token, a rate limit or a GitHub outage sent it down the create path, and a release that did exist was edited, and could have its assets replaced, without anything having established that it was still a draft. It now requires a confirmed absence to create, requires a confirmed draft to edit, and stops on any other answer before it changes anything.
- Fixed an upgrade reporting success when the daemon it restarted never came back. Teaching the installer that a live-but-unresponsive process counts as "running" made it count as "started" too, so a version that came up and never answered passed the health check the rollback depends on. Whether something is *there* and whether it is *answering* are now asked separately.
- Fixed the installer treating a daemon that is alive but not answering as stopped. `looptroop status --json` reports that case as `running: false` with the process id in a separate field, precisely so an installer does not read it as "nothing is there", and the installer read only the first field. An upgrade replaced the executable under a live process holding the port, then started a daemon that could not bind it. Both fields are now read.
- Fixed the installer accepting an empty or flag-shaped option value. `--prefix "$DIR"` with `DIR` unset installed the standalone executable into whatever directory you happened to be in, and `--version -h` asked GitHub for a release called `v-h`. The installer now applies the same three rules the release scripts do.
- Fixed a signal arriving in the instant after `install.sh` starts the installer but before it is ready to pass signals on, which killed the wrapper outright and left the installer running without it. The handlers are now in place before anything starts.
- Fixed the README telling you to choose an install directory with `--prefix`, which the npm installer refuses: that option applies only to the standalone executable. It now says how to move an npm install instead.
- Fixed the trusted-executable check being able to hand back a Windows command script, which the scripts using it cannot run without a shell: the WinGet submission runs on Windows and would have failed with an error naming nothing. It now refuses one and says which setting to point at the executable.
- Fixed an empty `WINGET_TOKEN` being accepted as a token, which corrupted every diagnostic the script printed. Three more settings that were read the same way, where a set-but-empty value would have been taken as real, are corrected with it.
- Fixed re-running the standalone installer deleting the previous version's backup while nothing was installed beside it. That is the state a failed rollback leaves, and its message tells you where that backup is, so the obvious next step destroyed the only working copy. Staging and rejected leftovers are still cleared.
- Fixed the two remaining release scripts that read their own arguments, so a misspelled flag on a job holding a publishing token is refused rather than ignored. `--force`, the one power the channel push is careful about, was read in a way a typo silently turned off.
- Fixed a failed rollback naming the wrong location for the rejected file once it had been put back.
- Fixed a failed rollback being able to leave no executable installed at all. Restoring the previous version is two renames, and if the second failed the good copy was left in quarantine with nothing in its place. The rejected file now goes back if the restore cannot, and the message says where both copies are.
- Fixed the installer failing to find npm on Windows. Node ships an extensionless `npm` shell script beside `npm.cmd`, and the installer's own PATH search preferred it, so every npm call reported that npm was not installed. Extensions now win, as they do on Windows itself, and a quoted PATH entry resolves too. The installer also distinguishes "npm could not be started" from "npm refused", instead of offering permissions advice for a program that never ran.
- Fixed installing on Windows from any account whose name contains a space. The installer reached `npm` through a command shell, and the shell re-read the command line, so a tarball under `C:\Users\Ada Lovelace\AppData\Local\Temp\...` arrived at npm as four separate arguments. The installer and the Chocolatey packaging steps now run the tools directly, and the one place that genuinely needs a shell (Windows batch shims such as `npm.cmd`) gets a command line with every argument quoted. The Chocolatey API key no longer passes through a shell process at all.
- Fixed `install.ps1` ignoring `-DryRun` and `-Help`. The installer has parsed `--dry-run` and `--help` for as long as it has existed, and `install.sh` passes everything straight through, but the PowerShell wrapper forwarded only four of the six options, so on Windows both did nothing at all. Both are now declared and forwarded, the usage text lists them, and it prints the PowerShell spelling of every option when that is the wrapper you used rather than always naming `install.sh`.
- Fixed every install leaving a temporary directory behind. `install.sh` ended by replacing itself with Node, which meant the cleanup it had registered could never run. Node also left its own download directory behind when interrupted, so a cancelled `--binary` install could leak an archive of about 110 MB. The wrapper now waits for Node instead of replacing itself, forwards interrupt, terminate and hangup to it, and reports Node's exit status as its own; Node removes its downloads when a signal arrives.
- Fixed `install.ps1` detecting a truncated download and saying nothing about what to do next. It now offers the same recovery as `install.sh`: download the installer and run it from a file.
- Fixed the standalone installer replacing the executable under a daemon whose state it could not read. `status --json` has three answers: running, stopped, and no answer at all. The third counted as stopped, so an upgrade could swap the file under a live daemon and never start it again, leaving the old version serving while `looptroop --version` reported the new one. The installer now asks such a daemon to stop, refuses only when the daemon says outright that it is still running, and starts it again afterwards. An installed copy that cannot even print its own version is treated as serving nothing, so a broken install can still be repaired by installing over it.
- Fixed a rolled-back upgrade leaving the new version's licences and notices behind. The standalone installer copied every non-executable file from the archive into the install directory before it checked the daemon, swapped the executable, verified the version and restarted. A failure after that point restored the executable and reported that the previous version was back, beside the newer version's files. Those files are now copied once the executable is installed and has proved that it runs.
- Fixed the download size limit being undone a moment after it was applied: the archive streamed to disk and was then read back into memory in full to check its checksum. It is now hashed in chunks. The smoke tests' health check is bounded by the timeout it is given, rather than only consulting it between attempts, so a daemon that accepts a connection and then stalls can no longer hold it open indefinitely.
- Fixed the standalone installer downloading with no timeout and no size limit. A connection that died silently looked exactly like an install still in progress, and a response was read into memory whole before the checksum could object to it. Release metadata and assets now abandon a transfer that stops making progress, refuse a body larger than the installer is willing to read, stream to disk rather than buffering, and delete a partly written file instead of leaving one for the next run to fail a checksum against.
- Fixed two installers in one directory being able to hold the same lock. Both could see one stale lock, both remove it, and both create their own, after which the second deleted the first's. A stale lock is now taken over through a rename, which exactly one process can win, and a lock is only ever removed by the installer that holds it.
- Fixed delivery stalling for two minutes on a machine whose only GitHub credential is a token in the environment. The branch push lends `git` the credential helper `gh` already has, but the push of the squashed candidate commit built its own settings and took the shared timeout and retry count without the credentials, so on a container, which is where a bare `GH_TOKEN` is normal, every `gh` call worked and that one push stopped to ask for a password it has no way to request. Ticket creation and delivery's remote fetches had the same gap and failed instead of stalling. All of them now use the same environment.
- Fixed `looptroop doctor` reporting a Node version as fine when the program would refuse to start on it. Anything from 24.15 passed, and so did the read-only install check, while the launcher required 24.18. Machines in that range could never run LoopTroop; they now find out from `doctor` rather than from a program that exits immediately.
- Fixed a nightly or release candidate of the minimum Node version passing for the minimum itself. `24.18.1-nightly.0` comes *before* `24.18.1` (which is how npm reads `engines.node`, and therefore how whatever installed that runtime read it), but the launcher and `doctor` compared the three numbers alone, so a build missing the fix the floor exists for started the app and failed somewhere unrelated.
- Fixed the launcher and `doctor` telling every user to install Node with nvm, which is not how anybody installs it on Windows and not how most people do on macOS. Both now name Homebrew, winget or a distribution package as appropriate, and always offer nodejs.org as well.
- Fixed the launcher telling a user on Node 24.18.0 to install Node 24.18.0. It compared only the major and minor parts and printed a zero patch level.
- Fixed the read-only install check misreading a Node path that contains a space, which is where Node lives on Windows by default. It split the whole line on spaces and took the second field as the version, so the check reported a version of `Files\nodejs\node.exe`.
- Fixed an approval screen discarding a draft that arrived a moment after the document. The interview, PRD and setup-plan panes restored as soon as the document landed and then latched, but the saved draft comes from a second request, so a slower one meant the pane restored its defaults, recorded them as the baseline, and dropped the real draft when it arrived. All three now wait for both, and Edit is unavailable until that restore has run.
- Fixed a failed setup-plan generation never restoring a saved raw draft or commentary, because restore waited on the parsed plan and a failed generation has none.
- Fixed an archived attempt's setup-plan pane saving an edit-mode change nobody made. The restored baseline recorded the value the draft asked for rather than the one the pane was showing, and because the pane is not remounted when the attempt clears, the autosave that switched on then wrote back a difference the user never introduced.
- Fixed the address bar being rewritten underneath an open dialog. Configuration, Prompts, New Project and New Ticket set the address themselves while another part of the app set it from the selected ticket, so refreshing on `/config` with a ticket open reopened the dialog and then replaced the address behind it, leaving Back with nowhere to return to.
- Fixed a link straight to a ticket being replaced by the ticket from your previous session before the first one had loaded.
- Fixed a link to a ticket this account does not have (deleted since the link was made, or copied from another machine) being answered with whichever ticket the previous session had open. The board is shown instead, and the address is corrected in place, so Back does not return to the broken link only to be corrected a second time. Back onto a ticket deleted while you were away is handled the same way.
- Fixed Back reopening a dialog you had just dismissed. Closing a routed dialog pushed the route it was restoring, duplicating the entry the dialog had opened over. Closing a dialog you opened from inside the app now pops that entry, so one Back after close leaves the ticket instead of requiring two.
- Fixed a link to a path this app has no screen for (`/nowhere`, `/ticket/`, `/ticket/new/extra`) opening the previous session's ticket instead of the board when a selection was still restored.
- Fixed `/ticket/LT-1/extra` and `/ticket/LT-1/` being left in the address bar. Extra segments on a ticket that exists are repaired to that ticket; a trailing slash on Configuration is repaired the same way.
- Fixed a deep link showing the previous ticket's dashboard until the ticket list loaded, so you could edit the wrong ticket while the address bar named the one you asked for.
- Fixed Back onto a real ticket while the list was still loading being treated as a deleted ticket and replaced with the board, and Back to the board in that same window leaving the previous ticket on screen until the list arrived.
- Fixed closing Configuration before the ticket list loaded writing the previous session's ticket into the address bar instead of the deep link you opened.
- Fixed the logo leaving an open dialog on screen. It wrote `/` itself, which the part of the app that owns the address immediately overwrote with the dialog's own route.
- Fixed the welcome and restore overlays sitting under the header, so the logo could be clicked through them and cancel a deep link that had not loaded yet.
- Fixed the address bar still naming a ticket that was deleted while you had it open. Closing a ticket that is already closed changes nothing the address correction watches, so the correction never ran and the address kept pointing at a ticket that no longer exists. The first correction of any session was skipped for the same reason: its counter started at the value that means "nothing to correct yet".
- Fixed an address this version has no screen for being left on screen. A typo, a bookmark from an older layout or a link from a newer version resolved to nothing and stayed in the address bar, so refreshing or sharing it repeated the dead end. It now shows the board and corrects the address in place, both on arrival and when Back lands on one.
- Fixed a link straight to a ticket being lost when a dialog opened before the ticket list had loaded. The address was read at the moment the list arrived rather than at the moment you arrived, so the dialog's own address was mistaken for the one you followed.
- Fixed clicking the logo being undone a second later. Going to the board is a decision; the address correction treated it as a page that had not settled yet and put back whatever had been open.
- Fixed the bead plan approval screen restoring its draft before the saved one had arrived. The interview, PRD and setup-plan panes were repaired earlier in this release; the bead plan had no such check at all, and it is now the same one all four use, required rather than assumed, because the previous form of it defaulted to "ready" and was therefore never exercised by any test.
- Fixed the setup-plan pane never restoring a draft again after you closed an archived attempt. Opening an archived attempt spends the one restore the pane allows itself, so returning to the live plan left your saved edits behind.
- Fixed an acknowledgment that failed to reach the server never being retried, so a ticket you had already looked at kept flashing for attention in every other tab and in the next session. It is re-sent on the next reading of the ticket, until the server confirms it. Clearing an acknowledgment the server was not holding is no longer sent at all: it recorded nothing and could not change anything, so it was re-sent on every poll for as long as the ticket stayed open.
- Fixed the step countdown showing the previous step's remaining time for up to a second after switching steps.
- Fixed a renamed file being committed twice. `git status --porcelain -z` reports a rename as two fields, and both parsers read only the first, so the bead commit staged the new path and not the deletion of the old one and the final-test audit never saw the file disappear. A copy's source is still not reported as deleted, because it is not.
- Fixed a failed bead commit leaving its files staged, where the next bead committed them by accident. The index is snapshotted and restored unless the commit succeeds. The Manual QA checkpoint commit is protected the same way.
- Fixed a bead diff reporting a git failure as an empty diff, which read downstream as a bead that changed nothing, and fixed it capturing LoopTroop's own control directories.
- Fixed the candidate rewrite discarding uncommitted work: it now refuses a dirty worktree before resetting.
- Fixed the squash path filter accepting `foo/bar/..`, Windows-style separators and drive-qualified paths. It feeds `git add -f` and `git checkout`, and was the weakest of the four copies of that rule; there is now one.
- Fixed a quoted or unreadable timestamp in OpenCode's own log aborting the rest of the file and returning a 500 from the combined log channel. An unreadable timestamp is now recorded as absent and sorted last rather than replaced with the current time, which had floated hours-old lines above everything.
- Fixed `channel=all` returning every native OpenCode row for a ticket's sessions regardless of the phase or attempt the request asked for.
- Fixed a malformed `Cookie` header answering 500 instead of the ordinary 401.
- Fixed the loopback check accepting any host starting with `127.`, including a hostname under someone else's control that merely began that way.
- Fixed `text/event-stream` being accepted as a request content type, which skipped both the type check and the 2 MiB body limit.
- Fixed ticket creation advancing the project's ticket counter outside the transaction that inserts the ticket, so a failed insert burned a number.
- Fixed a failed port bind leaving the WAL checkpoint and the live-event cleanup running with nothing able to stop them, and fixed two overlapping starts each running the startup sequence.
- Fixed two concurrent Manual QA evidence uploads or removals losing one another's entries. The index is now updated under a lock that holds across processes.
- Fixed a cancelled ticket keeping its work-budget ledger, its pending session continuations, and any question already part-way through being answered, the last of which had left the model with an answer, no receipt, and no resolve.
- Fixed a second answer-batch submission being accepted while the first was still running, which deleted the first's skip receipts on its way to failing. The batch's timeout is also derived from the ticket's configured AI budget instead of a flat ten minutes, so a slow but valid turn is no longer aborted. A claim left behind by a daemon that died is reclaimed the moment it expires, including at the exact instant of expiry: the one case where the ticket could report no holder and still refuse the next submission.
- Fixed council member variants being locked at ticket start without the canonical parser, so an invalid shape was stored and then read back as nothing, silently dropping the ticket's variants.
- Fixed orphan cleanup missing `question_waits` and `manual_qa_improvement_tickets`, whose surviving rows distorted wait accounting and pointed improvement mappings at deleted tickets.
- Fixed the pull-request phase claiming attempt 1 for its sessions on a restarted ticket.
- Fixed a failed message read looking like a completed turn with no output, a malformed tool part stopping the event stream, and a permission-reply failure being reported as a clean user cancellation.
- Fixed a child process reporting no process id being recorded as pid 0, which produced a status claiming a live server nothing could stop.
- Fixed a cancellation abandoning the wait for a health check or model catalog fetch without cancelling the request itself.
- Fixed a coverage follow-up budget of 0% still producing one question, so the setting could not be turned off.
- Fixed a Manual QA skip reason being lost on reload: it now belongs to the draft the autosave writes, and survives being read back.
- Fixed an approved execution setup plan's commands being rewritten for whatever host read them instead of the host recorded on the plan.
- Fixed git hook validation running without a usable snapshot and restoring only after everything had finished, so an abort or a failing hook left its changes in the worktree. The snapshot now covers the index too, so a hook that stages files no longer leaves them staged.
- Fixed a prompt started after its deadline receiving an apparently unbounded clock and running past the timeout meant to bound it.
- Fixed a bead dependency declared in one direction only passing pre-flight. The scheduler runs on `blocked_by` alone, so two beads that each declared they blocked the other both ran.
- Fixed the interface's execution setup plan serialiser dropping the copy-size metadata the generator measured and turning an explicit "allow large copy: false" into an absent field.
- Fixed the pull-request phase reading a stored Manual QA summary without validating it or refusing a failed outcome, which the integration phase already did, so the same run could be refused by one phase and described to a model by the other.
- Fixed Manual QA checklist generation repairing and retrying silently, leaving the operator with a generic notice and no sign anything had happened.
- Fixed a bead edit that touched only `prdRefs` or `contextGuidance` being dropped from the refinement change list while the bead file kept the new values. Both fingerprints read those fields now, and the winner-draft reader that hardcoded them empty reads them too.
- Fixed an interview document failure losing its diagnostic. The variable that should have carried the failing candidate's excerpt was declared, read, and never assigned, so the retry quoted the whole response instead.
- Fixed the Manual QA mandatory repository inspection accepting any completed tool call. It checked only that some tool finished, not which tool, not that it was read-only, and not that it touched the repository, so a single to-do write satisfied it. The tool must now be one of the read-only inspection tools the prompt allows, and any file or directory it names (including every entry of a list of them, and a Windows drive-letter path read on a Linux or macOS host) must stay inside the ticket's worktree. Each tool's arguments are read for what they are: a `glob` pattern is a location and is checked, a `grep` pattern is search text and is not, so searching the code for a literal `../` is still a real inspection. Argument names are matched however they are spelled, and a `read` that names no file is not evidence of anything. Both places that watched for it (the live stream and the finished messages) use the same check.
- Fixed a bead's stored status being reconciled on some read paths and not others. The board, the watch view and the ticket payload read the tracker separately and showed whatever an earlier release had written, and the prompt context and Manual QA evidence lookup each parsed the file by hand, where a single malformed line threw and lost the whole tracker. Every reader goes through the same one now, which skips a malformed line rather than failing the read; the board's own reader no longer blanks a ticket's whole bead list because one line was unreadable. A status whose only fault is its capitalisation (`Completed`, `DONE`) is also accepted from a model instead of costing a retry, which is what the read path already did with it.
- Fixed a Manual QA repair bead depending on a merge group that does not exist. The lookup was asserted, so a group id the model invented was stored as a dependency on nothing, which every later reader of the bead graph then had to survive. Unknown ids are dropped, and three other asserted lookups in the same function now say what is missing instead of failing later.
- Fixed Manual QA reading the approved PRD four different ways: a local schema plus a cast that the result did not satisfy, a second inline shape for requirement text, a third derivation for coverage, and fix-bead generation putting whatever text was on disk straight into a prompt. One reader now, with the minimal shape the feature actually needs, so a malformed PRD is refused everywhere rather than in two places out of four.
- Fixed interview coverage reporting `clean` while also returning gaps or follow-up questions. The clean status won, and every follow-up question beside it was then dropped in silence because the status was not `gaps`. It is a validation error now, retried like the PRD and beads coverage checks, which is the same check, written once instead of three times. If the retries run out and the answer still contradicts itself, the reported work is believed over the label: a `clean` result that lists gaps is read as `gaps` so the follow-up questions are asked, and a `gaps` result naming nothing to resolve is read as `clean`. A `gaps` status with neither a gap nor a follow-up question is rejected outright.
- Fixed a refinement retry quoting a reply that was cut off mid-sentence back to the model as though it were a schema mistake. A truncated reply is not a validation error, and the drafting step has treated it as its own kind of failure for some time; refinement now does the same and simply asks again.
- Fixed an interview batch being rejected for a repeated question id in a question that was about to be discarded. Batches are capped at three questions, and the check ran before the cap, so a fourth question could fail a batch whose kept part was perfectly valid.
- Fixed one unreadable line in a ticket's bead file hiding every other bead's test commands from workspace setup, which could then accept a workspace that cannot run them.
- Fixed a council round electing a different draft on two runs from the same scorecard. Two drafts tied on points were separated by the order their votes happened to arrive in, which is the order parallel models happened to finish. Council order decides now; the main implementer still wins a tie outright.
- Fixed the PRD and interview steps spending their retries on a winning draft that cannot be read. Only the bead step checked this up front, and the other two asked the model to rewrite a refinement when the thing that could not be read was the draft it was refining.
- Fixed the interview coverage result being saved with its written form and its parsed form disagreeing (the text saying `clean` while the reading said `gaps`) after the two were reconciled.
- Fixed a council round resuming on a winning draft that is nothing but whitespace. Recovery after a restart checked that the draft had content at all, which whitespace satisfies, and refinement then ran against an empty draft.
- Fixed a refined interview or PRD that returned no `changes` shipping an empty diff. The accounting was skipped entirely when the list was absent, so the canonical artifact could change while the attribution and the diff stayed empty. A refinement that differs from the winning draft is now accounted for: edits to a question or epic that kept its id are filled in automatically, and anything else fails validation and retries. The PRD check now compares the whole document rather than its epics and stories alone, so a rewrite of the problem statement, the scope, the technical requirements or the risks is reported instead of passing as unchanged; warnings distinguish reconstructed item-level changes from document-only edits. A coverage revision, which records its edits in `gap_resolutions`, is unaffected.
- Fixed bead refinement starting against a winning draft that does not parse. Refinement cross-validates against that draft, and the retry prompt asks the model to rewrite its refinement (not the draft that broke), so every attempt failed identically on the same input. It is refused up front now, before a model call is spent on it.
- Fixed coverage follow-up questions being read two different ways. The interview session carried its own narrower copy of the normalisation, so the same coverage response yielded a different question type, different options, and no option limits depending on which path read it. There is one normaliser now, with the session's own defaults passed in by name.
- Fixed a repeated question id overwriting the question that held it. Matching the source and round was enough to replace a question, so a new prompt could inherit the previous prompt's answer. A batch may still fill in metadata a compiled question lacks, but not contradict it, and a batch that repeats an id inside itself is rejected.
- Fixed selected options being stored exactly as sent. A single-choice question could keep several selections, a free-text question could keep selections at all, and an id naming no option was persisted and later shown to the model as a fallback label. Selections are checked against the question they answer, and the same checked result decides both the skip and what is written.
- Fixed a saved interview session being restored on the strength of four top-level fields. Everything else was asserted rather than checked, so a malformed artifact came back as a session holding whatever had been written into it. Every field and nested value is validated now, and a malformed session is refused with a diagnostic instead. Contradictions that need more than one field to see are caught too: two questions sharing an id are refused, because answers are filed by id and the second would have silently replaced the first; an answer belonging to no question is dropped rather than counted towards progress; and a saved selection that the interview screen would reject (a repeat, an option the question does not offer, two answers to a single-choice question, anything at all on a free-text one) is cleaned up rather than carried into the finished interview. Every restored answer is re-read for whether it is a skip, the way the interview screen reads one, so a blank saved as answered stops being counted as answered and keeps the time it was recorded. A batch question that reuses a known question's id while asking something else is refused, as is one that belongs to no question list at all: its answer would have been saved and then shown nowhere. So are progress counters, negative round numbers, and history entries naming a question that does not exist or naming the same one twice.
- Fixed a restored workflow snapshot keeping invalid values for bead progress, iteration counts, council results and dates. Each field is checked on its own now and falls back to its default with a warning, so one bad value no longer travels with an otherwise usable session, and no longer discards it either. Bead counters that cannot both be true (more beads finished than exist) are among them: the coding step reads that as "everything is done" and would have gone straight to final testing. A date that cannot be read is replaced with a real one rather than with an empty string.
- Fixed a repaired YAML scalar swallowing its own trailing comment. `free_text: answer # reviewer note` stored the comment as part of the answer, and the same text behaved differently depending on whether another line in the document happened to break parsing: a document that parsed dropped the comment, one that needed repair kept it. The comment is split off before quoting and put back unchanged, so both paths agree. A hash inside quotes stays part of the value.
- Fixed which alias wins when a payload names the same field twice. The lookup walked the payload's own key order and took the first match, so a document carrying both the canonical name and a legacy alias resolved by whichever the model happened to write first. The alias list is the precedence order now, and a disagreement is recorded as a repair warning naming the key that was ignored, once per disagreement, and on every path that resolves one: interview refinements, resolved interview documents, coverage follow-up questions, and both coverage revisions used to resolve aliases with nowhere to put the warning. A repair the parser applied is also reported as a repair, rather than being described in the warnings while the summary said none had run.
- Fixed the two exact-match copies of the alias lookup sharing a name with the normalising one, so searching for `getValueByAliases` could not tell you which of two behaviours a call site wanted. The exact-match version is one shared helper now, and it no longer answers to a key the record inherited rather than owns.
- Fixed repair warnings from a rejected candidate being reported against the one that validated. Four YAML repair steps also recorded their warning before the parse that was meant to justify it, so a repair that failed still appeared in the accepted result. Every repair step parses first now, and warnings are collected per candidate.
- Fixed two YAML repairs being applied without being recorded at all: inserting the missing space after a list dash, and removing duplicate mapping keys. Output rescued by either reported no repair.
- Fixed the interview question parser reporting a repair it had discarded. It ran two inline-syntax repairs, threw the result away, parsed the original text, and reported the repair anyway. The parser now says which text it actually used.
- Fixed a ```jsonl code fence being unwrapped one character short, leaving a stray `l` at the start of the payload and failing the parse.
- Fixed the vote score bounds being written out in five places. The parser's upper bound, the voting prompt's rubric and its scoring instruction each carried their own copy of 20 and 100; they now read one pair of constants. The parser also holds the 100-point total the prompts promise, rather than trusting that five categories capped at 20 can never add up past it, and the retry prompt restates that ceiling alongside the per-category one.
- Removed a duplicated `single_choice` clause in interview answer-type normalisation; underscores are already stripped before the comparison.
- Fixed a completion marker naming one bead finishing another. The report's `bead_id` was read, returned, and then ignored: any valid marker accepted the running bead as done. A marker for a different bead is now a validation error that retries.
- Fixed "was the marker there?" being inferred from the error text. Any validation error that was not the missing-marker message read as though the tags were present, so a prompt echo looked like a well-formed report that failed validation. The bead completion and final-test parsers now compare against the real tags, which the final-test parser had never been passed.
- Fixed a stored bead status the scheduler does not recognise stalling a ticket forever. It only runs `pending` beads and only finishes when all of them are `done`, so a `complete` or `todo` left over from an earlier release was a bead that never started and a ticket that never ended, with nothing said anywhere. Bead status is now checked when it is parsed, and reconciled with a warning when it is read back off disk. `iteration` is clamped to a whole number of at least one instead of being stored as `NaN`.
- Fixed a quoted `"false"` making a setup command mandatory. `required` was read with `Boolean(...)`, which is true for every non-empty string, and serialisers quote scalars often. It is read with the boolean parser now, and a value that parser cannot read is a validation error rather than a guess.
- Fixed duplicate final-test file effects hiding a disagreement. The first entry for a path won and the rest were dropped, so the same file could be listed as a temporary artifact and as something to commit with only one of those surviving. Identical duplicates merge with a warning, and a real conflict fails validation.
- Fixed council winner selection seeding itself from the first council member. An empty scorecard, or an all-zero one that did not include the main implementer, elected a model whose draft carried no votes; the three refine steps then looked that draft up with a non-null assertion and worked on `undefined`. Only a scored draft can win now, ties still go to the main implementer, and a round with nothing scored fails with a message instead. The four places that looked up the winning draft say which phase and which model when the lookup misses.
- Fixed an empty refinement reply being replaced by the winning draft. The validator then saw a well-formed document with no changes, accepted it, and the structured retry never ran. An empty reply is now a validation failure that retries on a fresh session, and the session log records what the model actually returned.
- Fixed a phase recovered after a restart trusting the winner id in its persisted vote artifact. A corrupt or partial artifact was assigned unchecked and threw inside the refine handler; the recovery now fails cleanly so the run takes its existing "intermediate data lost" retry path, and requires the recovered winner to have a completed draft.
- Fixed bead refinement being accepted when the winning draft could not be parsed. It returned the model's raw change list with an advisory warning, and the callers treated that as validated output. It is a retryable validation failure now.
- Fixed beads refinement retries falling back to the generic correction prompt. The beads-specific one, which spells out the bead schema and the rule that every changed bead appears exactly once, existed but was never passed. Reading a persisted beads refinement, beads coverage revision or compiled interview back off disk is also checked now rather than cast, at every site that reads one, not just the first.
- Fixed a deleted ticket's saved-panel revision outliving it. The revision only ever climbs, so reusing the id made every autosave on the new ticket claim to replace a revision that never existed, and the server refused each one as a conflict.
- Fixed cancelling a ticket with "also delete it" leaving everything cached. That path really deletes the row but answers with only a success flag, so none of the deletion cleanup ran.
- Fixed a refused project deletion leaving every ticket in that project unable to save panel state until the page was reloaded.
- Fixed a panel save queued behind a stalled one still reaching the server after the ticket was deleted, once the deletion stopped waiting for it.
- Fixed a queued panel save still being able to start after a deletion began, and a stalled one being able to hold the deletion open forever. Deletion now closes the door on new saves and waits a bounded time for those already in flight, on the project path as well as the ticket path.
- Fixed project deletion missing tickets the browser knew only by id: one whose details were still loading, or that appeared only in an artifact or saved-panel entry. A ticket id carries its project, so all of them are found now, including a request in flight that would otherwise have reinstalled the ticket after the delete.
- Fixed a create or update response skipping the ticket normaliser, so a caller reading the result directly got the raw server shape.
- Fixed a response carrying part of a ticket's runtime replacing all of it. A reply with a bead count alone would blank the bead list, the pull-request state and the estimate until the next refresh.
- Fixed a status-only response leaving the previous status stale when the ticket was open on the board but its detail had never been loaded.
- Fixed the draft screen reading the stored council roster without checking it, the third and last surface still doing so.
- Fixed ticket ids being pasted into request URLs unencoded. Ids come from the project's issue tracker, so an id containing a slash asked the server about a different route entirely and one containing a question mark truncated the path, and roughly half the call sites encoded while the other half did not. Every request that names a ticket, project, phase, bead, Manual QA version or evidence file now encodes each part of the path.
- Fixed queries continuing after the view that asked for them was gone. Ticket lists, ticket details, interview questions, saved panel state, artifacts, Manual QA, projects, prompts, the profile, startup status and update checks now stop with the component that started them, instead of running to completion and writing their result into a cache nobody is reading.
- Fixed a prompt save rejected by validation being treated as a success. The editor refetched the catalog and the prompt afterwards, and the reset that follows a refetch discarded the draft the person was still correcting.
- Fixed the project form treating a refused git check as a verdict, the same way the folder picker did.
- Fixed a mutation response being able to put a malformed field into the ticket cache: a status that is not text, or a runtime that is not an object, is now dropped rather than carried through.
- Fixed a malformed entry in a phase's version history being used to pick a version.
- Fixed the folder picker treating a refused git check as a verdict. A 500 while checking a directory produced a confident "not a git repository", the same wrong answer an out-of-order response gave.
- Fixed the approval screens letting a PRD or bead plan be approved while the coverage check had failed. An absent coverage warning reads exactly like "no gaps", so the button said "Approve" and the answer had never been obtained; it now says why it is unavailable and waits.
- Fixed the council and phase-review screens showing artifacts and logs from the live attempt when the version history failed to load; the version being shown was unknown, and it may not have been the one selected.
- Fixed a failed request being drawn as an empty result. A server error while loading a bead list, a phase's attempt history, a beads or setup-plan or PRD outline, a per-bead diff, the read-only view of an approval artifact, or a phase's logs produced the same screen as "this has not been generated yet", so nothing indicated a failure, and nothing offered to retry. Each surface now names the failure, quotes the status the server sent, and offers a retry. A phase whose logs failed to load is no longer recorded as loaded-and-empty, which had made every later request for it serve that empty snapshot instead of asking again.
- Fixed a failed request for a phase's version history hiding the version selector, which silently scoped artifacts and logs to the live attempt on the council, phase-review, approval and coding screens.
- Fixed a failed setup-plan request rendering as "plan generation failed", which offered a destructive Regenerate for a plan that may well exist.
- Fixed the artifact list showing a failed request as a phase that produced nothing; the notice used to live inside a dialog nobody opens for an empty button.
- Fixed the PRD approval screen hiding a failed refresh whenever it still had older content cached, so stale text stayed editable and approvable with no warning.
- Fixed the attempt list treating an unexpected payload as "one attempt". A response that was not a list read as no archived attempts at all, which hid the version selector on a phase that had been retried.
- Fixed the read-only approval view requesting interview answers for PRD and bead attempts. It called the interview endpoint whichever artifact was open, so opening an archived bead plan cost a request that says nothing about beads, and reported its failure over the bead plan.
- Fixed a failed bead-metadata request blanking the labels it had already loaded, which silently downgraded named per-bead commits to bare ids.
- Fixed Manual QA fix beads looking like ordinary beads outside the coding view. The ticket normaliser dropped `qaOrigin` and `completedAt` from each bead, so the origin badge never appeared in log grouping and the completion time was lost, even though both were on the payload and on the type.
- Fixed the board and the phase timeline disagreeing about bead progress: the card preferred the ticket's own bead columns while every other surface preferred the live runtime projection. All of them now read the runtime, which already falls back to those columns when the server sends no runtime.
- Fixed a half-formed Manual QA origin reaching the origin card, which indexes into its evidence and links without guarding. An origin that cannot produce an evidence link is now no origin rather than a crash.
- Fixed an expired session going unnoticed while the live stream retried. The first failure of a connection now asks an ordinary API route whether the session is still good, and only a refusal from that signs the tab out; an unreachable daemon or an ordinary disconnect does not.
- Fixed the council roster stored on the configuration being read without checking. Both the Configuration screen and the ticket header parsed it inline and asserted the result, so a stored effort setting that was not text reached a badge, and a roster that was not a list reached code expecting one. It is now parsed and validated in one place, and the ticket header no longer parses it while rendering.
- Fixed deletion leaving per-ticket data behind. One rule now clears everything cached under a ticket id rather than an enumerated list of six query families that a seventh silently escapes. In-flight requests are cancelled before the entries go, so a response already on the wire cannot bring a deleted ticket back, and a queued panel save is allowed to finish before the ticket is deleted rather than reaching the server afterwards. Deleting a project now finds tickets recorded only by having been opened, not just those in the cached list.
- Fixed a ticket acknowledgment from an earlier ticket with the same id suppressing the new one's error and needs-input flashing. A legacy "seen" marker counted as acknowledgment for any signature; nothing has written it for some time.
- Fixed the folder picker acting on answers for a folder you have already left. Neither the directory listing nor the git check was cancelled when you navigated, so a slow answer could arrive last and decide whether "Select This Folder" was enabled, for a folder nobody was looking at.
- Fixed questions lingering on tickets that are finished or no longer listed, which left an answer-and-skip affordance for a step nothing was waiting on, and let the panel's dismissal and timer bookkeeping grow for the life of the tab. A question that disappears without an explicit resolution is now dropped as soon as the step reports its remaining set, rather than up to thirty seconds later.
- Fixed the question poll restarting every ten seconds. It depended on a set rebuilt by each ticket-list refetch, so it tore down its interval and re-fetched every open question each time, whichever tickets were active.
- Fixed a slow per-ticket question refresh arriving after a newer one and pruning questions that were still live.
- Fixed a historical error rendering with no logs at all. The error list runs newest-first, but the code that bounds a failure's time window read the "previous" error backwards and took the newer one, so the window ended before it started. Undated lines used to slip through and hide it; excluding them, as this release does, made it visible.
- Fixed the error view falling back to the *oldest* unresolved error rather than the most recent, which put its recovery actions beside the wrong failure.
- Fixed the live-stream session check running on every reconnect. A daemon that was simply down was asked about the session every three seconds for as long as the tab stayed open; it is now asked once per connection, and again only after a stream has successfully opened.
- Fixed a slow question refresh overwriting a newer poll, or a question that had just arrived live, and pruning it; the ordering was only enforced in one direction.
- Fixed a slow poll for waiting questions overwriting a newer one, or a newer per-ticket refresh, and pruning questions that were still live.
- Fixed a question countdown jumping on every open ticket when a late timer frame arrived: the frame was rejected for display but still moved the shared clock correction.
- Fixed the error view offering recovery for an error that had already been resolved: while a ticket is blocked, the error it shows is now the one still open, and the remembered selection is used for reviewing history. "Edit setup plan" now appears after any setup failure, not only one that blocked from preparing the environment; the surrounding text already described both the same way.
- Fixed an error occurrence with no recorded time being stamped with the current time during rendering, which reordered the list and churned its keys on every pass; it now uses the ticket's own last-updated time.
- Fixed undated log lines from the whole phase being pulled into a failure's time window.
- Fixed a status-only response from a ticket action leaving the previous status stale, which is what several screens read to explain what failed.
- Fixed a saved panel's revision being recorded during rendering rather than when it was fetched. React's development double-render alone wrote it twice, and the value decides which revision the next save claims to be replacing.
- Fixed Escape inside a nested overlay closing the surface behind it. Every dialog, menu and picker in the app dismisses itself on Escape and lets the key travel on, so the same keypress that dismissed "Cancel ticket?" also left the ticket, the one that dismissed the folder picker also closed the Projects window, and the one aimed at a model list closed the whole Configuration window instead. Escape now belongs to whatever is open on top: a dialog, an alert dialog, a menu, a listbox, a combo box, a focused dropdown, any Radix popper, or an event something else has already handled. The two pickers that portal their popup outside the page, where none of those checks can see it, stop the key themselves, and the model list, which previously had no Escape of its own, now closes and hands focus back to the control that opened it.
- Fixed Back leaving the About overlay floating over the board. About has no address of its own and sits above everything else, so browser navigation closed the Configuration screen underneath it and left About over nothing. It now closes with a Back or Forward, and with the Configuration screen it was opened from.
- Fixed the keyboard-shortcuts overlay opening underneath everything else. It sat below the ticket view, the About window and both dropdown popups, so `?` opened a help panel nobody could see, and once that panel held the keyboard and made the rest of the page inert, the interface simply stopped responding until Escape. A popup left open behind it is now inert like the rest of the page, instead of staying in the overlay's keyboard path.
- Fixed the keyboard-shortcuts overlay advertising `n` for a new ticket and `k` for the board. Neither was ever bound, so pressing them did nothing and the shortcuts that do work lost credibility with them. The list now holds only `?`, Escape and `/`.
- Fixed the header's refresh spinner turning for the rest of the session when the refresh failed, which reads as "still working" rather than "that did not work".
- Fixed a refused clipboard write (a denied permission, or a page not served over a secure connection) reporting success. Copy now reports whether it worked, the "Copied" tick only appears when it did, and a refusal straight after a successful copy takes the previous tick down instead of leaving it standing, unless it is an older attempt settling late, which no longer disturbs a newer one. Copying a whole log says so when it fails, which it had stopped doing.
- Fixed a prompt save that lands while you are still typing replacing what you typed. The stored copy still arrives, and the editor now absorbs it without putting the older text back on screen. A result is also no longer reported against a prompt you have switched away from, in either direction; the editor is one instance for every prompt.
- Fixed a prompt's saved status and warnings disappearing a moment after a save. Saving invalidates the prompt, the server copy comes back changed, and the editor treated that as somebody else's edit and reset itself, so a save with warnings looked like a save with nothing to say. The editor now recognises its own save rather than comparing text, which matters because the stored copy is re-serialised and rarely matches what was sent byte for byte. The feedback stands until the next edit, prompt switch or revert, and a save the user has already typed past no longer reports itself against the newer draft.
- Fixed a prompt save or revert that never reached the server saying nothing at all. A refused request left the editor looking as though nothing had been asked of it; it now reports what went wrong and keeps the draft.
- Fixed a failed edit of an interview answer going only to the browser console. The editor closed, the rewritten answer was discarded, and the old one stayed on screen looking saved. The editor now stays open with what you wrote and says why it did not save.
- Fixed ticket cards being unreachable without a mouse. The card was a plain box with a click handler, so nothing on it could be focused or activated from the keyboard, and the name it carried for screen readers was on an element they do not announce as a control. The title is now a real button, named after the title it displays and then the ticket id (the whole card still opens the ticket when clicked), and the nested controls inside the card stay separate controls, which they could not have been had the card itself claimed to be one.
- Fixed the filter bar's Reset ignoring the search box and hidden mock tickets. The button vanished while the board was still filtered by either, and pressing it left the search in place, so "Reset" did not reset.
- Fixed presets deleted from triage coming back on the next load. Presets from an older per-scope storage format were merged in on every load, and the merge only lost to a name that still existed, so a preset you deleted was copied back out of the old key, however many times you deleted it. Those keys are now retired, but only once the merged set has actually been stored: deleting them first and then failing to write, in a private window or against a full quota, would have destroyed the only copy. A write that is refused leaves them queued instead of forgotten, so the next change that does reach storage retires them; otherwise a deletion made after a failed write would be undone on the following load; the same applies to a key storage refuses to delete. The recovered presets are added to the record as it stands at that moment rather than to the copy the tab started with, so a second tab's change is not overwritten by the one step here that cannot be undone. A browser that refuses to list stored data at all no longer stops the interface from starting.
- Fixed a Manual QA choice being frozen into a ticket at the moment it was created. The new-ticket form starts out inheriting from the project and configuration, and resolved that to a fixed yes or no on the way out, so a later change to either never reached the ticket even though the form had said "inherit". It now sends the inherited state, as the AI-question fields beside it already did.
- Fixed renaming an environment variable in an execution setup plan destroying another one. A rename was a delete followed by an insert, so renaming `FOO` onto an existing `BAR` dropped `FOO` and overwrote `BAR`; the row also jumped to the end of the list on every keystroke and the field was rebuilt under the cursor, taking focus with it. Rows now hold their place and each remembers the name it occupies in the plan, so a name another variable already has is reported rather than applied: nothing is renamed or dropped behind you, and every other edit on the form still reaches the plan while you sort the collision out. A name a row still holds counts as taken even after the field is cleared, and a cleared field says which name it is still saved under. Freeing a name applies whichever rename was waiting for it, so resolving a collision the obvious way (ask for the taken name, then move the row holding it) leaves the plan matching the form. Two names that differ only in case are pointed out: Windows treats them as one variable, so only one of them would reach the command there.
- Fixed a board card acknowledging a wait once and never again. Whether a card had been seen was decided when the column was first drawn, so a ticket that later started a different wait (a bead approval, a new question) kept the answer worked out for the previous one and never pulsed for the new one.
- Fixed the disk allocation bar in ticket details rendering an invalid width for a ticket that occupies nothing, which left the bar at whatever width the previously viewed ticket had.
- Fixed the model picker's provider rows and the file tree's folder rows being expandable by mouse only, and the search field's focus timer surviving the dropdown that scheduled it.

- Fixed a coding run with an OpenCode step cap destroying the project's own `opencode.json`.
