The cap now merges into readable project configuration through the durable writer and restores ordinary non-conflicting runs. A conflicting current file is preserved with its valid sidecar, and destructive reset or recovery refuses to overwrite it; a cap-created file whose original was absent keeps that marker while an edited file remains visible for deliberate recovery. Missing ownership evidence is never guessed.
- Fixed the temporary step cap being committed onto the ticket's branch or lost during a reset. A valid cap marker keeps the root config out of bead and final staging, while safe resets reapply the cap. Edited, deleted, or malformed sidecar state leaves the marker and capped config visible instead of guessing ownership; unknown hook-created untracked paths are also retained when protected validation cannot attribute them safely. Protected hook-validation markers live in owner-only application data, and recovery compares tracked, staged, and untracked state before restoring the exact saved index, so a later edit cannot be overwritten by a stale crash snapshot.
- Fixed startup recovery guessing at interrupted writes. Recovery now scans only known config and ticket artifacts, recognizes current temp names, validates JSON and whole-file JSONL completeness, and requires a byte-length/SHA-256 `.proof` for YAML. A fallback copy uses an exclusive no-follow target and a durable `.recovery` ownership marker. Ordinary orphan YAML without proof and torn whole-file JSONL are warned about and left unpromoted; only an in-progress fallback whose ownership or completeness marker cannot be verified raises `RecoveryBlockedError` before projections, hydration, or timers, preserving the affected files. Legacy temp names, symlink temps, unknown artifacts, and oversized or unreadable files remain visible with diagnostics.
- Fixed Manual QA durability gaps across baselines, drift receipts, evidence indexes, and event history. Owner-only contained writes now use exact path and symlink checks, evidence locking uses a persistent SQLite transaction database, and invalid JSONL event shapes are warned and retained with their raw line for diagnosis. Startup recovery preserves unresolved fallback sidecars at the point it blocks, while ordinary unproved files stay visible with warnings rather than being promoted.
- Fixed opening a different ticket inheriting the previous ticket's workspace. The workspace was re-rendered with new data rather than rebuilt, so everything the screen was holding stayed put: interview answers and per-question skip reasons, the Skip All dialog and its reason, a pending AI question's skip form, a Manual QA round's pass/fail marks and observations, which round you were looking at, the description editor and its unsaved text, a failed start's notice, and the error screen's retry note. Two tickets in the same phase looked identical, so there was nothing on screen to say the text belonged to the ticket you had just left; and autosave then wrote it to the ticket now in front of you. Each ticket's workspace is now built from scratch, and a test drives the real screens through a switch to keep it that way.
- Fixed saved workspace state loaded for one ticket being restored onto another. A ticket's saved drafts arrive after its screen does, so a reply still in flight when you switched used to be applied to whatever was on screen by the time it landed, and then autosaved there. Saved state now says which ticket it was loaded for, and is only ever restored onto that one.
- Fixed a ticket's log history being replayed from a stale snapshot. Logs already fetched were cached for the lifetime of the browser tab and never refetched, so leaving a ticket and coming back showed the lines as they were when you left; everything that arrived in between was missing until a reload. Nothing was ever dropped from that cache either, so it grew for every ticket visited. A ticket's cached logs are now released when you leave it, and fetched again when you return. A request still in flight at that moment is discarded rather than allowed to refill the cache it was released from, which is what would otherwise have handed the stale snapshot straight back.
- Fixed a queued AI-details refresh firing against a ticket you had already left. The delay that batches model metrics outlived the screen that scheduled it, so metrics arriving as you switched refreshed the wrong ticket a moment later. Leaving a ticket now settles that delay immediately for the ticket that earned it, instead of abandoning it: model details are held for half a minute, so a refresh simply dropped would have left you looking at metrics from before the event if you came back inside that window.
- Fixed unsaved answers being wiped by a ticket's own saved state arriving. Anything typed in the moment before the saved drafts landed was overwritten with what was on disk, which for a ticket with nothing saved yet meant an empty form. What you have typed is now kept when there is nothing saved to restore, and counts as unsaved, so the next autosave stores it.
- Fixed an answer typed in the third of a second before you switch tickets being lost. Autosave waits for a pause in typing, and a switch inside that pause cancelled the pending save. It is now completed as the screen is left, against the ticket it was typed for.
- Fixed interview drafts being keyed without the ticket they belong to. Draft answers, per-question skips, selected options and skip reasons were filed under source, round and batch alone, so two tickets at the same point in an interview shared every key. The keys are on disk and stay as they are; the screen now clears its own drafts when the ticket changes rather than relying on being rebuilt around them.
- Fixed the reload that recovers a ticket whose data disappears never arming for a ticket you return to. It tells a first load apart from a ticket that had rendered and then lost its data, and it was tracking that per screen, so now that each ticket's workspace is built from scratch, a ticket revisited after its data was dropped looked like a first load and simply sat there loading. The record is now kept for the browser tab.
- Fixed a saved Manual QA draft arriving after the round being ignored. The round is often already cached while the saved draft is still on the wire, and the view committed to the round's own copy the moment the round appeared, so pass/fail marks, observations and evidence links saved earlier were dropped. It now waits for the saved draft before deciding what the round's draft is, and still falls back to the round's copy if that request fails.
- Fixed an unanswered AI question ending the run as a bare `Timeout`, with nothing in the record naming the question that caused it.
- Fixed a question left pending when the daemon restarted never being resolvable again. Sessions survive a restart, so a question whose session came back keeps the clock it had: a countdown you stopped stays stopped, one still inside its window keeps the time it had left, and one whose wait ran out while the daemon was down is refused straight away instead of being given another five minutes. A question whose session did not come back is refused, and now leaves a receipt in the ticket's Skips panel naming the restart, so a council round that lost a member to one can still be explained afterwards.
- Fixed time spent waiting on you only being counted once you answered. The wait is now recorded as it happens, so a question open right now already shows as waiting rather than as coding, and a restart in the middle of one no longer discards everything before it.
- Fixed a second question in the same step being ignored by the browser. Clocks are now identified individually, so a step that asks, is answered, and asks again shows the new countdown and can still be stopped; previously the page kept showing the clock that had already gone.
- Fixed the board not re-alerting when one question was answered and another arrived in its place. The count was identical and the ticket's status had not changed, so nothing looked different.
- Fixed a skip reason typed for one model's question following you to another model's tab.
- Fixed a wait left open by a daemon that stopped mid-question never closing, which would have counted the rest of the ticket's life as time spent waiting on you. Startup now closes any wait nothing is still waiting on.
- The AI questions panel now remembers whether you collapsed it, per ticket and per browser.
- Fixed switching a duration setting from Inherit to Custom showing an empty box that asked for a number of minutes, while the override it had just created was already saved and valid.
- A refusal OpenCode will not accept, and a failure to expire a question, are now written to the log instead of being swallowed silently.
- Fixed answering or skipping a question leaving the ticket's clocks stopped forever. The question was told to OpenCode but never closed out here, so the step never resumed, the question stayed on screen, and a skip left no receipt.
- Fixed a restart in a project with two active tickets refusing the wrong ticket's question. Questions are read per project but were reconciled per ticket, so every ticket's turn saw its siblings' questions as ownerless. Tickets whose sessions had all been abandoned were skipped entirely, leaving their questions hanging in OpenCode with no trail.
- Fixed being unable to type a multi-word answer. Every keystroke was trimmed, so a space vanished as soon as it was typed and the next word ran into the last one. Free text that happened to match one of the offered options was also silently dropped.
- Fixed a duplicate question event pushing the deadline out by another full window, which a repeating stream could do indefinitely.
- Fixed an answer that failed to send returning the question to a clock that had already run out, leaving it waiting with nothing left to refuse it.
- Fixed the browser never sending Stop for the second question on a ticket, so a countdown could run out while somebody was answering it, and fixed a new countdown being discarded as stale because the previous one had reached a higher revision.
- Fixed a ticket staying in Needs Input on the board after its question was answered elsewhere or refused by the clock.
- Fixed a screen reader reading the countdown out once a second. It now announces what the clock is doing rather than what it currently reads.
- Fixed auto-approval saying yes to `doom_loop` and `external_directory` on tool policies that deny them. Rules were read first-match, so the blanket allow was found before the policy's own override.
- Fixed a refused question's receipt reporting the whole wait as time the model spent working, which was the opposite of the rule the wait is built on.
- Fixed a skip reason surviving a change of mind. Undoing a skip, typing an answer, or picking an option now discards the reason, so it cannot re-attach itself to a later skip made for an entirely different reason.
- Fixed a cancellation reason being stored and then impossible to read. It is now shown on the canceled ticket, which matters most in the case it was built for: cancelling with the artifacts deleted, where the column is all that survives.
- Fixed the reason given for skipping all remaining interview questions never appearing anywhere. It is stored against the action rather than any single question, and the panel was hiding exactly that row.
- Fixed skipping the rest of an interview re-recording questions that had already been skipped in an earlier batch, which replaced their original entries with a decision made at a different time for different reasons.
- Fixed a failed interview batch leaving behind entries for skips it had rolled back. Retrying with different answers no longer contradicts a record of something that never happened.
- Fixed the Skips panel overlapping the AI details panel when both were open.
- Fixed the Skips panel showing state from up to thirty seconds earlier when it was already open as a skip was recorded.
- Removed Vite's native-config compatibility warnings from build and test runs by using explicit TypeScript extensions for local config imports.
- Fixed every streamed log line re-requesting the page it arrived on. The log context published its rows and its callbacks as one object, so it was a new value on every render and the panels listing it in their effect dependencies asked for the phase again per line. The rows and the callbacks are now separate: an effect that loads a page depends on the loader, whose identity never changes, and a view that draws rows depends on the reader, whose identity changes when the rows do and at no other time.
- Fixed the Full Log recopying and re-sorting every log bucket on the ticket whenever a loading flag changed rather than when the rows changed.
- Fixed the coding view appearing to freeze during streaming model output. It followed the number of log rows, and a streaming answer arrives as repeated updates to one row whose text grows, so the count never moved. It now follows the tail of the log itself. Its pending scroll frame is also cancelled when the view closes.
- Fixed a retried phase showing one merged attempt in its archived history. Log entry ids are unique only within an attempt, so two attempts that both recorded the same milestone folded into a single row. Restored pages now use the same identity the live overlay already used (attempt and fingerprint, not the bare id), and the log views key their rows on it too, so the attempts stay apart on screen as well as in the data.
- Fixed the archived log keeping the wrong copy of a row that was fetched twice. Pages are held oldest-first and were being folded backwards, so an older copy overwrote a newer one: a model answer whose first fragment and finished text landed in different pages showed the fragment. The restored row also keeps the time it started rather than the time it finished, so it stays where it belongs among the events that happened while it was streaming. Undated archived rows were also listed newest-first inside a log that reads downwards.
- Fixed two separate undated events with the same text being treated as one and the second discarded. A missing timestamp says nothing about when something happened; a row that really is delivered twice still collapses.
- Fixed the walk that loads a bead's complete log history continuing after you switched to another bead or closed the view, and restarting immediately after a failed page instead of stopping. The walk is now owned end to end: it is no longer interrupted and restarted by its own progress, which is what made a refused page look like a cancellation and let the retry loop run anyway. A refused page stops that bead's walk for as long as you are looking at it and no longer for the rest of the session; coming back to the bead tries again. The Full Log's "go to top" is owned the same way, down to the tab it was started on, and a page it cannot load no longer fails silently in the background.
- Fixed a log export asking the database for a ticket's entire history in one statement. It now walks it in pages. The exported text is unchanged, and there is still no cap: the panels treat that endpoint as the complete record. For the same reason an export that loses its ticket midway now fails outright rather than returning the part it had reached.
- Fixed a cancelled ticket showing an empty log. Its view never passed the ticket to the log panel, so no durable history was loaded.
- Fixed a finished ticket still showing a live activity line above its log, counting elapsed time against a run that had already stopped. A cancelled or completed ticket's last phase is no longer treated as the one currently executing.
- Fixed a per-model log tab rendering empty when the rows behind it named their model through the log source rather than a model field. The tab list and the filter behind it now agree on what identifies a model.
- Fixed a live event stream that had been replaced (by switching tickets, or by a reconnect) still acting on the ticket that replaced it. A late error closed the live connection, refetched the wrong ticket and started a reconnect nobody asked for; a late message could move the new ticket's resume position to an event id belonging to the old one. Every callback a connection installs now checks it is still the current one, and a connection queued as the view was closing no longer opens.
- Fixed the blueprint refinement prompt listing council votes among the context it is given. Nothing assembles votes for any step, so no model has ever received them, while both the preview in the Prompts window and the editable copy of that prompt showed a votes section that never arrives. The context key itself stays, with its label and its builder, so a future step can ask for votes by listing it.
- Fixed `looptroop logs` corrupting non-ASCII output. The tail is read backwards in 64 KiB chunks and each chunk was decoded on its own, so whichever character straddled a boundary became two replacement characters. `--follow` had the same fault across its per-change reads and now writes bytes straight through.
- Fixed a cancelled ticket leaving its OpenCode health probes running. The callers raced the probe's promise, which abandons the wait but not the request, and never handed it the cancellation signal, so a cancelled run kept a probe alive against an unreachable server for its whole timeout. The pre-flight connectivity check, the model-reachability check, the interview's opening health check and session creation all pass it now, as does the provider listing inside the probe itself.
- Fixed pending session continuations outliving the ticket that created them. They were cleared only when a ticket's sessions were aborted, so a ticket that completed naturally kept them for their full thirty-minute life and a restart under the same id reapplied the finished run's extra retry attempts.
- Fixed a second answer batch being accepted for a ticket that already had one in flight when it arrived on the fast path (a coverage batch, or mock mode), which cleared the in-flight batch's skip-receipt bookkeeping on its way past. Both submission paths now take the same claim, and the rollback state belongs to the call that created it rather than to a shared per-ticket entry.
- Fixed a bead tracker entry being cast to a bead rather than checked. Readers reach into a bead's dependencies, context guidance and test commands with no guard, so a row whose field held the wrong kind of value crashed a later step far from the file that caused it. Every known field is now type-checked when it is present; a row that simply has not reached a later stage of its life is still accepted.
- Fixed the line numbers reported for a damaged JSONL file counting only the lines that parsed, so blank and malformed lines shifted them and an operator was pointed at a record that was fine.
- Fixed git hook validation losing what it found to a failure in its own cleanup. The restore runs after the commands whatever happened, and an exception there replaced the validation result; a failed restore is now reported beside that result, and blocks under either policy. Validation is also refused outright when the index half of the snapshot cannot be taken, rather than run with no way to undo a hook's `git add`.
- Fixed a git operation running without the index snapshot that is supposed to undo it. When the snapshot could not be taken the work went ahead anyway, which is exactly the case it exists for: staging succeeds, the commit fails, and nothing can put it back.
- Fixed a lock left by a process that overran being reclaimed by a waiter and then deleted by the original holder on its way out, letting a third writer into a section the second was still inside. Each acquisition now carries a token and only removes the lock while that token is still the one on disk.
- Fixed the file-size metadata LoopTroop measures for an execution setup plan's workspace inputs being dropped the moment the plan was read back, so an edit saved from the interface came back without it.
- Fixed a stored execution setup plan's project commands being re-quoted for whichever machine opened it. The plan's own recorded host was already honoured for its steps, probes and hooks; project commands were the one field still asking the running host.
- Fixed a coverage follow-up budget inventing one follow-up for an interview with no questions to follow up on.
- Fixed repository-relative paths accepting a Windows drive qualifier without a slash. `C:notes.txt` is relative to the current directory on that drive, which is not the worktree, and it reached the filter that stands in front of `git add` and `git checkout`.
- Fixed the Manual QA checklist view showing nothing about the retries and repairs that produced it. Generation records them; the view now reads them, including for a generation that gave up and produced no checklist at all.
- Fixed a command that outlives its timeout hanging its caller when the process tree survives the kill. Both command runners waited for the child's `close` event, which only fires once every pipe is closed, so a surviving grandchild meant the promise never settled; Windows, where the kill is delegated to `taskkill` and its failure is invisible, is where it showed. They now give up shortly after the force-kill and report the timeout with whatever output arrived. This is the same bound the git runner already had; it was fixed there and not here.
- Fixed the candidate rewrite overwriting local files. Relaxing its pre-reset check to tracked changes was right (Manual QA and the final-test audit deliberately leave local-only output), but `git reset --hard` writes over whatever is on disk wherever the target commit carries that path, with no warning and nothing to recover from. Ignored build and cache output counts, and is the common case. The rewrite now names those files and refuses.
- Fixed the Manual QA repair notice appearing only on the artifact panel of the generating step, which is not the screen anyone is on while running the checks. It now appears on the Manual QA screen itself, for the round the latest generation produced.
- Fixed the Manual QA retry count reading one too high after a generation gave up.
- Fixed an answer batch that never finishes locking a ticket out of every later submission. The claim was released only when the background work settled, so work that ignored the cancellation held it for the life of the process.
- The mark that says an answer batch is being processed now lives in the project database instead of one daemon's memory. Two daemons opened on the same project could both accept the same submission, and restarting mid-batch forgot the mark entirely. It carries an expiry, so a daemon that stops while holding one no longer leaves the ticket unable to accept answers.
- Stopping LoopTroop while it is still starting now stops it completely. Shutdown resolved against whatever had been set up at that instant, and startup carried on afterwards to bind a port and start timers that nothing could then close.
- Fixed two daemons on one project both accepting the same answer batch. The claim decided from a read taken before its write, and the databases use a transaction mode where both readers see the same free slot; the write itself is the decision now.
- Fixed packaging a ticket overwriting local files a second way. The step restores every file the branch added after resetting, and that overwrites whatever is on disk just as silently as the reset does.
- Fixed skipping the remaining interview questions while an answer batch is still being processed. The batch would finish, fail, and undo the skip.
- Fixed a renamed file being missed when the rename had not been staged yet, which left the original path out of the commit and out of the audit.
- Fixed Git hook validation deleting your own untracked files when it could not list them. It now refuses to run rather than guess what was already there.
- Fixed `looptroop logs --follow` holding back the last lines written while it was mid-read, until something else was written.
- Fixed the Manual QA screen describing a checklist generation that gave up as one that completed, and not showing its repair trail at all when no checklist was produced.
- Fixed a bead tracker row whose field is present but half-formed being accepted and then crashing a later step: an empty `dependencies` object still broke the scheduler, and a Manual QA provenance record without its source items still broke the evidence loader. A field that is there is now checked as far as its readers go into it.
- Fixed a repository whose approved profile lists the same Git hook twice always reporting hook drift at integration.
- Fixed council loading throwing on a malformed stored model-variant value instead of falling back.
- Fixed a startup failure before the network bind leaving the write-ahead checkpoint and the live-event cleanup timer running with nothing able to stop them. Only the bind itself was guarded.
- Fixed the shared status lookup answering for names it does not know. A handful of them (`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`) came back with a member inherited from every JavaScript object instead of nothing, and callers check the answer for presence and then read a phase's fields out of it. Every lookup now goes through the same "is this a real status" check.
